cohort: 206 pregnant women admitted into the labor ward with singleton live pregnancies at a tertiary health facility.
finding: Pathological admission CTG findings were significantly associated with a higher frequency of adverse neonatal outcomes, including low birth weight, SCBU admission, asphyxia, neonatal death, and prolonged hospital admission, compared to normal or suspicious CTG findings.
mod_finding: All women with pathological CTG results had a cesarean delivery, while vaginal delivery was more common with normal CTG findings.
